Preserve the exact English short meaning supplied by generated-roots. Latin brevis supplies brev; the contraction brev|extensor independently establishes this boundary. Morphemes narrows its gloss to short (time), but brevicaudate/brevextensor show spatial shortness too; do not import that narrower gloss.

MW explicitly attests brevi- as a combining form meaning short, from brevis. Preserve family meaning short. brev and brevi are overlapping aliases of the same supported component: abbreviate and breviary boundaries use checked Latin endings; brevity additionally uses MW evidence that the historical -itas contains an adjective-stem i. Historical-stem indexing does not require a unique modern English segmentation.

Morphemes labels breve- a prefix, but checked evidence establishes Latin neuter breve and the English noun, not a productive English combining form. The apparent breve in brevextensor crosses brev|extensor. Do not add this form without independent component evidence.

Engra calls the descendant brief a root and supplies a Chinese gloss. The checked English headword is historically related, but adding a whole descendant solely to match its derivatives would change the root criterion. Keep its five candidates as related_only; short remains the selected family meaning, not a translation of the engra gloss.

records.sense_constraint: To shorten or reduce a word/name to a shorter form.
records.note: MW gives Latin abbreviatus/abbreviare from brevis; its -ate entry identifies the borrowed ending -atus. The retained i is before that supported ending, and MW independently attests brevi- from brevis. The analysis ab|brevi|ate is therefore a morphological inference from checked etymology plus suffix evidence, not a dictionary-printed segmentation or a substring-only match. brev is an alias of the same component. Initial ab- is assimilated ad-, not away.

records.sense_constraint: Past participle/adjectival use of abbreviate: shortened.
records.note: Verified-base inference: engra lists this under abbreviate; MW lists abbreviated as the verb inflection. The ordinary -ed formation preserves the base component. No separate abbreviated headword etymology was checked.

records.sense_constraint: A shortened written form, or the act/result of abbreviating.
records.note: The checked headword defines the act/result of abbreviating. The separately checked abbreviate entry establishes brevis ancestry; the brevi boundary is inferred from that base and its Latin -atus ending, not separately printed in the noun entry. The noun retains the component, with brev as its lookup alias.

records.sense_constraint: An agent that abbreviates.
records.note: Verified-base inference: MW lists abbreviator as a noun under abbreviate and engra places it directly below that base. Agent-noun formation preserves brevi. This is not a separately checked abbreviator etymology. Its erroneous child microbrewery is not inherited.

records.sense_constraint: The vowel/syllable mark and the musical note; the musical name preserves historical shortness despite its modern duration.
records.note: MW derives breve from the neuter of Latin brevis. The stem brev is supported; final -e is part of the inherited inflected form, so this word alone does not establish an English combining form breve-.

records.sense_constraint: Rare anatomical noun: a short extensor muscle.
records.note: The Century Dictionary, printed p.676, right column below brevetcy, explicitly identifies a New Latin contraction of brevis extensor and marks it rare. The supported boundary is brev|extensor. Its fifth letter e belongs to extensor, so the overlapping string breve is not a root match.

records.sense_constraint: A short summary or the historically abbreviated liturgical office/book.
records.note: MW gives Latin breviarium from brevis; its -ary entry independently identifies Latin -arium as the corresponding suffix. Thus i precedes the verified ending in brevi|arium and survives in brevi|ary. This is a morphological inference combining the checked etymology, suffix entry, and attested brevi- form, not a dictionary-printed segmentation. brev and brevi denote the same supported component.

records.sense_constraint: Zoological adjective: having a short tail.
records.note: The Century Dictionary, printed p.677, left column, and Maggenti/Gardner, printed p.143, both give the headword with Latin brevis and cauda. MW independently attests combining form brevi-. This is brevi|caudate, with brev as an overlapping alias of the same component.

records.sense_constraint: Short duration or conciseness of expression.
records.note: MW gives Latin brevitas from brevis; its -ity entry traces Latin -itas to adjective-stem -i- plus -tas. Under the collection's historical-stem lookup policy, both brev and brevi index this same supported component. Modern English brev + -ity analysis can coexist with the historical brevi stem. The brevi edge is an inference combining these checked entries, not a claim that the brevity headword directly labels its formation brevi-.

records.sense_constraint: The adjective short/concise and its historically related noun/verb senses.
records.note: MW traces adjective brief through Anglo-French brief/bref to Latin brevis and the noun through the summary/document sense. It is a historical relative whose modern spelling lacks brev or brevi. Do not promote the whole descendant brief to a new root merely to admit it.

records.sense_constraint: Comparative of adjective brief, or an agent noun of verb brief.
records.note: Verified-base inference: engra places briefer under brief. The requested MW briefer URL displays the brief entry and lists briefer as a noun, not an independent etymology. Both transparent readings retain the changed brief spelling, so they remain historical relatives of brev.

records.sense_constraint: Verb participle or a session/report that gives concise essential information.
records.note: Verified-base inference from checked verb brief plus engra ancestry; MW lists briefing among verb forms. No separate briefing headword etymology was checked. The -ing derivation retains brief and has no literal supported brev/brevi component.

records.sense_constraint: For a short time or in few words.
records.note: Verified-base inference: ordinary brief + -ly, supported by engra parentage. The base was checked, not a separate briefly etymology. The historical v-to-f spelling development prevents placement under brev/brevi.

records.sense_constraint: The quality of being brief.
records.note: Verified-base inference: brief + -ness; MW lists briefness under the adjective and both engra entries attach it to brief. This is run-on/base evidence, not an independent headword etymology, and the spelling remains brief.

records.sense_constraint: A small beer brewery.
records.note: The checked microbrewery entry concerns beer production; brew is traced to Old English breowan. Transparent micro- + brewery morphology supports exclusion from Latin brevis. The engra path abbreviate > abbreviator > microbrewery is a misplaced tree edge, not a derivation.
